from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import combinations
import json

# Part (a): any seven sum < 16 ?
# Sorted a1<=...<=a10. From a1+a2+a3 > 7 we get a3 > 7/3, and a3 is the
# smallest of the top seven, so every a4..a10 >= a3 > 7/3.
# Hence the seven largest sum > 7*(7/3) = 49/3 > 16, so (a) is impossible.
lower_a3 = F(7, 3)
lower_seven = 7 * lower_a3
a_possible = not (lower_seven >= 16)

# Part (b): any five sum < 12 ?
# Witness: all ten numbers equal t with t = 47/20.
# Check every 3-subset sum > 7 and every 5-subset sum < 12 exactly.
t = F(47, 20)
nums = [t] * 10
min_three = min(sum(c) for c in combinations(nums, 3))
max_five = max(sum(c) for c in combinations(nums, 5))
b_possible = (min_three > 7) and (max_five < 12)

final = []
final.append("a) No" if not a_possible else "a) Yes")
final.append("b) Yes" if b_possible else "b) No")

result = {
    "final_answer": "; ".join(final),
    "evidence": {
        "a_lower_bound_a3": str(lower_a3),
        "a_lower_bound_seven_sum": str(lower_seven),
        "a_possible": a_possible,
        "b_witness_value": str(t),
        "b_min_three_sum": str(min_three),
        "b_max_five_sum": str(max_five),
        "b_possible": b_possible,
    },
}
print(json.dumps(result))
